Spatial cross-validation for GWR-SCAD and GWR-MCP

Source: R/nonconvex-cv.R
cv_gwr_nonconvex.Rd

Evaluates a common decreasing lambda path using held-out spatial blocks. Standardization and nearest-neighbor construction are repeated inside each training fold, preventing transformation and neighborhood leakage.

Usage

cv_gwr_nonconvex(
  x,
  y,
  coords,
  k,
  fold,
  kernel = c("bisquare", "gaussian", "exponential", "tricube", "boxcar"),
  bandwidth = NULL,
  lambda = NULL,
  n_lambda = 50L,
  lambda_min_ratio = 0.001,
  penalty = c("scad", "mcp"),
  gamma = NULL,
  standardize = TRUE,
  screening = TRUE,
  metric = c("rmse", "mse", "mae"),
  refit = TRUE,
  control = gwrs_control(),
  cv_cache = NULL
)

cv_gwr_scad(x, y, coords, k, fold, ..., gamma = 3.7)

cv_gwr_mcp(x, y, coords, k, fold, ..., gamma = 3)

Arguments

x

Numeric design matrix without an intercept.

y

Numeric response vector.

coords

Optional coordinate matrix used to construct neighbors.

k

Number of neighbors when `neighbors` is not supplied.

fold

User-supplied spatial fold labels, one per observation. Create a reproducible assignment with [spatial_folds()] or supply application- specific blocks/buffers.

kernel

Spatial kernel.

bandwidth

Fixed distance bandwidth. The default `NULL` uses the farthest retained neighbor as an adaptive bandwidth at each target.

lambda

Decreasing vector of nonnegative regularization strengths. When `NULL`, a logarithmic sequence is generated from [gwr_sl_lambda_max()].

n_lambda

Number of automatically generated values.

lambda_min_ratio

Ratio of the smallest to largest generated value.

penalty

Nonconvex penalty, either `"scad"` or `"mcp"`.

gamma

Concavity parameter. The default is `3.7` for SCAD and `3` for MCP. SCAD requires `gamma > 2`; MCP requires `gamma > 1`.

standardize

Whether predictors are standardized globally before the local fits. Coefficients are returned on the original scale.

screening

Whether to use sequential screening. A full KKT scan is always performed, so screened variables that violate optimality are restored before a solution is accepted.

metric

Criterion used for selecting the final pair: root mean squared error (`"rmse"`), mean squared error (`"mse"`), or mean absolute error (`"mae"`). All three are returned.

refit

Whether to fit the selected model on all observations.

control

Numerical controls from [gwrs_control()].

cv_cache

Optional read-only preparation from gwr_nonconvex_cv_cache. Inputs must match exactly; responses and penalty paths are not cached.

...

Additional arguments passed by [cv_gwr_scad()] or [cv_gwr_mcp()] to `cv_gwr_nonconvex()`.

Value

An object inheriting from `gwrs_nonconvex_cv` and `gwrs_cv`.

Details

With the guarded-block solver, a lambda is eligible only if all held-out observations have finite, converged predictions. Otherwise all its error scores are `NA`; no observation is removed. `cv$observation_count` retains the planned full denominator and `cv$valid` reports eligibility. If none are valid, the object has zero rows in `best`, a `NULL` fit and a warning. Refit uses the existing single-lambda initialization, not the CV path's warm start, and is independently checked for convergence.

Examples

quake <- datasets::quakes[1:30, ]
coords <- as.matrix(quake[, c("long", "lat")])
x <- as.matrix(quake[, c("depth", "stations")])
fold <- spatial_folds(coords, n_folds = 3, seed = 42)
cv <- cv_gwr_mcp(
  x, quake$mag, coords, k = 8, fold = fold,
  lambda = c(0.12, 0.04), refit = FALSE,
  control = gwrs_control(n_threads = 1, diagnostics = "none")
)
cv$best
